arguments.title: Remove recommended_next/Next Up from ticket board show to match ticket-mcp board_show parity
arguments.description:
`ticket board show` (CLI) currently bundles the draftboard snapshot with a `recommended_next` array, a `Next Up` human section, and recommendation-driven `Immediate Actions` text ("Start open X next"). `ticket-mcp` `board_show` only returns the raw draftboard snapshot (no recommendations), while a separate `ticket-mcp next_tickets` / `ticket next` call surfaces the same ranked candidates. This asymmetry makes CLI and MCP `board show` behave differently for the same underlying board state.

Since `ticket next` (CLI) and `next_tickets` (MCP) already provide the recommendation surface, drop `recommended_next` / `Next Up` from `ticket board show` entirely so both interfaces' `board show` only reports board/WIP state (active/stale/conflict entries, file ownership, warnings) and never ticket recommendations.

Scope:
- `workflow-tools/ticket/src/cli/commands/board.rs`: stop calling `cmd_next` from `build_board_display`; drop `recommended_next` from the JSON payload; simplify `build_actions` to no longer reference recommended tickets (keep conflict/stale/wip_limit actions; drop the "Start ... next" / "When you free capacity ..." branches that depend on recommendations).
- `workflow-tools/ticket/src/cli/commands/board/render.rs`: remove `BoardRecommendation`, `board_recommendation_to_json`, `write_next_up`, and the `recommended_next` field from `BoardDisplay`; stop calling `write_next_up` from `render_board_human`.
- Update affected tests in `workflow-tools/ticket/tests/integration_board_cli.rs` and `workflow-tools/ticket/tests/integration_board_cli/*.rs` that assert on `recommended_next`/`Next Up`.
- Update the cross-interface best-next-ordering spec (`memory-api/.spec/specs/ec22fe34-2d24-4dc5-a067-85121bed3655/body.md`) to remove the requirement that `board show` expose recommendations, and state that `board show` is board-state-only while `next`/`next_tickets` is the sole recommendation surface on both CLI and MCP.

No change intended to `ticket next` / `ticket-mcp next_tickets` behavior.

        priority: value

            .unwrap_or("none")
            .to_string(),
        effort: value

            .map(str::to_string),
        dependency_count: value
            .get("dependency_count")
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .unwrap_or(0) as usize,
        dependee_count: value
            .get("dependee_count")
            .or_else(|| value.get("dependees"))
            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
            .unwrap_or(0) as usize,
        became_actionable_at: value

            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .map(str::to_string),
        created_at: value
            .get("created_at")
            .and_then(Value::as_str)
            .unwrap_or("-")
            .to_string(),
    })
}

arguments.explanation: Update the best-next-ticket spec: board show no longer surfaces recommendations; next/next_tickets remain the sole recommendation surface

replacements.newString:
The ordering contract applies to:

- `ticket next`
- `ticket-mcp` `next_tickets`

`ticket board show` (CLI) and `ticket-mcp` `board_show` (MCP) are board-state-only surfaces: they report active/stale/conflict entries, file ownership, and warnings, and must never embed ticket recommendations (`recommended_next` / `Next Up`) or duplicate the `next` ordering. `next` / `next_tickets` are the sole recommendation surfaces on both interfaces, keeping CLI and MCP `board show` behavior identical.

No dedicated ticket-http `next` or board recommendation endpoint exists today, so HTTP is out of scope unless a future surface exposes the same workflow.

- CLI and MCP must apply the same ordering contract for equivalent candidate sets.

- `ticket next` and `ticket-mcp` `next_tickets` must not embed a second board snapshot; `board show` remains the single board surface, while `next` surfaces only candidate data plus board-aware exclusions or warnings when relevant.
- `ticket next` and `ticket-mcp` `next_tickets` items must surface the derived numeric `dependee_count` field.
- Default non-JSON `ticket next` output must render its candidate `items` using a compact labeled card format that prioritizes rank, short ticket id, and title, while preserving next-specific metadata like `count`, `warnings`, and `excluded_by_board`.
- The CLI `ticket board show` `Immediate Actions` section must not describe or name a specific ticket to start; when the board is clear it directs the caller to run `ticket next` to see unblocked tickets instead.
- Tool descriptions and user-facing contract text must describe the actual ordering keys.
